learnings.symptom: Make scenario metadata can report status=paused and isActive=true at the same time, so one status field cannot safely prove whether a scenario is an active mutator, callable service, frozen legacy path or retirement candidate.
learnings.rootCause: Make metadata fields describe different lifecycle/runtime concepts and are not a single canonical activity truth.
learnings.failedApproach: Infer ownership, cutover or retirement from one Make status field.
learnings.provenFix: Determine operational activity from scenario metadata plus trigger/scheduling/webhook state, recent execution evidence and readback of actual callable/mutation behavior.
learnings.regressionContract: No ownership/cutover/retirement decision may rely on status or isActive alone.

learnings.symptom: BG139/BG186 showed tightly clustered executions and a 429 organization rate-limit event; five near-simultaneous BG139 runs each started the same BG190 fallback.
learnings.rootCause: Concurrent identical Mission Control requests can independently traverse cache miss/fallback paths without single-flight/request coalescing.
learnings.failedApproach: Allow every concurrent cache miss to launch its own fallback/read/write chain or add more retry/watchers.
learnings.provenFix: Use a stable single-flight key for the Mission Control snapshot so one caller resolves cache/live fallback while concurrent callers reuse the result; preserve bounded retry and explicit stale/miss semantics.
learnings.regressionContract: Concurrent equivalent Mission Control requests must not create multiple equivalent live fallback chains or duplicate projection writes.

learnings.symptom: Historical BG190 execution evidence showed a direct ACTIVATE call into BG186, bypassing the BG191 promotion gate.
learnings.rootCause: Projection write capability and promotion authority were not separated strongly enough at the write boundary.
learnings.failedApproach: Let a live fallback worker both write shadow state and promote that state to ACTIVE.
learnings.provenFix: Current BG190 configuration uses WRITE_SHADOW; BG191 remains the promotion route and promotion evidence must be independently verified.
learnings.regressionContract: Any BG186 ACTIVATE effect without authorized BG191 promotion evidence is UNAUTHORIZED_PROJECTION_ACTIVATION and cannot produce GREEN_VERIFIED.

learnings.symptom: BG139 accumulated a queued webhook backlog while incoming browser/portal GET requests arrived in a repeating pattern consistent with multiple periodic callers; inspected deliveries originated from browser contexts rather than a Make retry loop.
learnings.rootCause: More than one client-side polling consumer appears to call the same Mission Control webhook without shared cadence/coalescing.
learnings.failedApproach: Blindly resume/activate the queued webhook scenario before deduplicating callers, which can release the backlog as a burst.
learnings.requiredAction: Trace portal/frontend callers, reduce to one canonical polling owner where polling is still needed, coalesce equivalent requests, and perform a queue-safe canary before restoring normal throughput.
learnings.regressionContract: A queued Mission Control webhook with unresolved duplicate caller evidence must not be blindly activated into an uncontrolled burst.

learnings.symptom: BG139 can intentionally serve a stale cache record within a grace window.
learnings.rootCause: Availability fallback semantics can be confused with current verified production truth if freshness is not carried explicitly to consumers.
learnings.provenFix: Expose source, freshness, verified_at/valid_until and production truth separately; stale cache may serve degraded availability but cannot imply current GREEN_VERIFIED evidence.
learnings.regressionContract: CACHE_STALE cannot be projected as unconditional healthy/current state.
